_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Support Equipment Installation Data (SEID)
summary: The SEID provides the Government with information required for installing support equipment in existing or planned shipboard or shore-based facilities, including space, mounting, environmental, and safety requirements.
description_purpose:
3.1 The SEID provides the Government with information required for the installation of SE in existing or planned shipboard/shore-based facilities.
3.2 It includes services, as well as space, mounting, environmental, special facility, and safety requirements relating to SE installation.
application_interrelationship:
7.1 This data item describes data required by MIL-STD-2097(AS), paragraph 5.6.2.10.
7.2 This DID shall be applied to SE intended for installation in shipboard and/or shore-based facilities.
7.3 DID DI-ILSS-80118A, LSA-070, SERD is related and companion data.
7.4 This DID supersedes UDI-P-21006D.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Reference Documents.
preparation_instructions.content: The applicable issue of the documents cited herein, including their approval dates and dates of any applicable amendments, notices, and revisions, shall be as specified in the contract.

preparation_instructions.title: Content
preparation_instructions.content: SEID shall be furnished as required in MIL-STD-2097(AS), paragraph 5.6.2.10. The SEID required shall be legible and sufficiently detailed to enable site layout, preparation, and complete installation of the equipment by the procuring activity. The data shall include items of information as listed in paragraph 10.3.

preparation_instructions.title: Items of Information
preparation_instructions.content:
The items of information required shall be prepared under the following headings:
a. Equipment Physical Requirements.
b. Space Requirements.
c. Mounting Requirements.
d. Servicing Requirements.
e. Safety Requirements.
f. Security Requirements.

children.title: Equipment Physical Requirements.
children.content: List as follows:

children.title: Envelope dimensions
children.content: List length, width, and height of equipment, excluding packaging. If equipment folds for storage, list both storage and operating dimensions.

children.title: Weight
children.content: List weight of equipment, excluding packaging.

children.title: Space Requirements.
children.content: List as follows:

children.title: Operator space
children.content: List space required by personnel for operation of the equipment.

children.title: Drawer removal space
children.content: List space required for removal of drawers, opening of doors, or removal of access panels, if applicable.

children.title: Access space
children.content: List access space required at front, rear, above, below, and each side of the equipment.

children.title: Additional space requirements required for units under test (UUTs) or ancillary test equipment.

Indicate storage requirements for ancillary test equipment and related publications.

Safety Requirements.
children.content: The provisions and equipment necessary to protect personnel and equipment including sound attenuation and laser requirements shall be stated.

children.title: Security Requirements.
children.content: State the security classification of the equipment being installed or the classification of any equipment used with the installed equipment.

children.title: User Voltage.
children.content: The nominal user input voltage (AC) is defined as the root-mean-square (rms) voltage applied. The nominal user input voltage (DC) is defined as the actual positive or negative voltage applied.

children.title: User Voltage Tolerance
children.content: is the maximum permitted departure from nominal user voltage during normal operations, excluding transient and cyclic voltage variations.

children.title: Transient Voltage Tolerance.
children.content: A voltage transient (excluding spikes) is a sudden change in voltage which goes outside the user voltage tolerance limits and returns to and remains within these limits within a specified recovery time after the initiation of the disturbance. The transient voltage tolerance is in addition to the user voltage tolerance limits.

children.title: Transient Voltage Recovery Time
children.content: is the time elapsed from initiation of the disturbance until the voltage recovers and remains within the user voltage tolerance limits.

children.title: Phases.
children.content: Shipboard generators generally have their alternating-current circuits arranged to produce three-phase a.c. power with an angular relationship of 120 degrees. Single-phase a.c. power is also available aboard ship.

children.title: Nominal Frequency
children.content: is the steady state, nominal user input frequency in Hertz (Hz).

children.title: Frequency Tolerance
children.content: is the maximum permitted departure from nominal frequency during normal operation, excluding transient and cyclic frequency variations.

children.title: Steady State Current
children.content: is full load current in rms amps drawn by the user equipment.

children.title: Start-Up or In-Rush Current
children.content: is the turn on, peak current drawn by the user equipment.

children.title: Duration of In-Rush Current
children.content: is the time (in milliseconds) from sudden change in current (turn on) until the current recovers to steady state value.

children.title: Harmonic Current Spectrum
children.content: is the user equipment line currents from the 2nd up to 32nd harmonic (expressed in percent of the fundamental current). A harmonic frequency is a multiple of the fundamental frequency.

children.title: Connected Load
children.content: is the nameplate rating of all equipment in the systems.

children.title: Steady State Operating Load
children.content: is the continuous steady-state power in kW and kVA consumed by the user equipment.

children.title: Transient Operating Load
children.content: is the sudden change in power (kW and kVA) consumed by the user equipment.

children.title: Power Factor
children.content: is the ratio of total watts per phase to the total rms volt-amperes per phase.

children.title: Leakage Current
children.content: is the total rms current that passes from phase to ground with nominal voltage impressed at the nominal frequency.
